events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Many have asked my opinion on a possible Russia-NATO conflict.
This is going to annoy many people, and hopefully give them a reality check, but my opinion is very simple.
1. Russia had some valid strategic and ideological reasons for what it did in Ukraine, regardless of whether I condone the invasion or not. Was it successful? Arguably yes, arguably no—it depends on what you consider as the war’s key objectives. The war actually pushed two neutral countries into NATO and pulled Ukraine even further away from Russian influence.
2. Russia does not have any valid strategic reason to invade the Baltics or any other NATO territory. Any attack on the Baltics cannot be excused as ‘protecting Russian culture & language’ or fighting ‘Nazism’. If this does happen, it’ll be a clear sign of expansionism, nothing more and nothing less. Russia is not a saintly country and I don’t put it past them. 
3. If Russia does miscalculate and invade NATO territory, it will backfire spectacularly and the Russians will be bogged down within weeks. A clear victory is unattainable for either side and things will spiral out of control.
4. NATO is being underestimated by the ziggers. Even without U.S. boots on the ground, European nations pose a significant threat to any Russian advances, and in my opinion, countries like France, Poland, Sweden, and so on should not be dismissed. Even Germany, which is often ridiculed by pro-Russian commentators, should not be dismissed in case of war.
5. A land war with NATO will therefore, in my opinion, not take place (unless the Russians are retarded). The only thing I possibly see happening is massive drone attacks against Eastern European nations such as Poland or the Baltics. In this aspect of warfare, Russia clearly holds the quantitative advantage & can pressure NATO strongly. But over time, just like with Ukraine, the strategic cost of such a conflict will become too high, and ordinary Russians will feel it.

I am not happy about the reignition of the Ethiopian civil war.
They say the war reignited in three different territories and it is coordinated attacks, airports got seized, local governments got couped, overall. it is going to be a very shitty day.
I, of all people, should be happy. Were it the Federal Government that told Kenyan officials that "Egyptian special forces were on the ground", or those who denigrated us continuously in the media, with some on their TV openly saying they have no issue taking away our water from us?
All nations have some people who have bottomless malice in their hearts, yet they are still people all the same, why should I be happy that another one or two million people are going to die, and twice that number will be orphaned and double that be traumatized for their lives?
I helped Ethiopians find work, I shared bread and salt with some of them, and for a time politics was not part of our world, we became friends and coworkers, afterall, we share a continent and we must learn to live away from the madmen of ethnic supremacists and political fanatics. 
Yet, peace is not meant to be, the Feds will be fighting against the rebels and the locals, probably to the bitter end this time, the horror show will go on. At some point war is inevitable, let us hope it will be the final one.

🚨Russia hits Ukrainian intel data hubs and logistics nodes
Russia's Armed Forces struck a series of high-value targets across Ukraine on Wednesday, the Defense Ministry reports.
📍In Kiev, drone strikes destroyed the United DS data center, which handled data processing, transmission, and international communications for Ukraine's special services. A second Kiev facility — the New-Telco data center, a key internet traffic exchange hub for Ukraine's Defense Ministry — was also hit.
📍In the Odessa region, strikes took out two logistics centers in Odessa and Ilyichevka, that were used for storing and distributing military cargo flowing in from European states.
The operation targeted data centers, logistics hubs, and warehouse terminals supporting the Ukrainian military's operations.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🤥Trump’s Gaza plan gets bogged down amid Israeli political and funding hurdles
US President Donald Trump’s Board of Peace is set to unveil a $2.45 billion recovery plan for Gaza, but has yet to secure the full sum, Axios reports.
Board of Peace officials claim donor countries would fund the plan’s 66 projects once key political hurdles are cleared.
➡️ A major obstacle is Israel. While it has agreed in principle to the plan’s agenda, it has refused to implement it, citing domestic political concerns and the ongoing election cycle.
The October 27 Israeli elections may fail to produce a clear winner, with Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar party increasingly challenging Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud. A post-election deadlock could further delay implementation of the Gaza recovery plan.
Meanwhile, Hamas has agreed to hand over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee, but the process remains stalled as Israel refuses to withdraw from Gaza and implement a 14-day ceasefire.
👉 Flattened by Israeli strikes, Gaza’s reconstruction needs far exceed the $2.45 billion plan: physical damage is estimated at $35.2 billion, while full recovery could cost around $71.4 billion over the next decade.
The Board of Peace comprises dozens of member countries and is overseen by an Executive Board that includes High Representative for Gaza Nickolay Mladenov and former British Prime Minister Tony Blair. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and White House envoy Steve Witkoff are expected to attend the September 23 meeting.
👍 [Substack](https://geopoliticsprime.substack.com/) | [Chat](https://t.me/+HLrnOk92f31mYzIy) |
